title: Adaptive Route Eviction State Machine for Automatic Fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive, per-route state machine that fuses overload signals (429 rate, request timeouts, 5xx error-rate spikes, queue-depth) and reliably triggers staged fallback actions and circuit-like protections. The state machine should be tenant-aware, support probation/decay for recovery, and emit rich telemetry for observability.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Per-route state machine installed behind the router for a canary subset of routes. 2) Detects 429/timeouts/error spikes within configured windows and executes staged actions (soft rate-limit, concurrency reduction, model-variant swap to a lower-cost compatible variant, regional redirect) with observable transitions. 3) Includes hysteresis and exponential backoff to avoid oscillation. 4) Emits transition events and metrics to Console (per-route trip_score, active_state, last_trigger_reason). 5) Rollout plan to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback on measurable regression in latency or error-rate.
design_notes: - Signal fusion: combine 429 rate (+weight), timeout count, tail latency P95, and queue saturation into a trip_score. - Windowing: 30s fast window + 5m smoothing window. - Thresholds: default trip_score thresholds are configurable per-route/tier. - Staged actions: (1) soft degrade (reduce concurrency limit by 25%), (2) switch to cached response policy or degraded model variant, (3) regional fallback if available, (4) open circuit (reject/queue with 429) if persistent. - Decay & probation: after action, require sustained healthy windows before full restore. - Tenant isolation: per-tenant rate limits and probation so noisy tenants don't take down variants. - Safety caps: never route to a variant lacking required features (function calling, streaming) unless explicitly allowed by route config.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype trip_score aggregator (server-side) and expose metric. 2) Build state machine library with clear states: Healthy, Probation, SoftDegrade, VariantFallback, RegionalFallback, OpenCircuit, Recovering. 3) Implement action handlers (concurrency throttle, model-pinning override, regional redirect signal). 4) Wire telemetry and Console events. 5) Canary rollout on internal routes and 3 customer routes, gather telemetry for 2 weeks. 6) Iterate thresholds and hysteresis parameters.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit metrics: route.trip_score (gauge), route.state (enum), route.last_trigger (string), route.probation_start_ts, route.open_reason, route.fallback_variant. Create Console dashboard with per-route timelines and a high-signal alert when >5 production routes enter OpenCircuit within 10m. Add automated safety action to pause rollouts if canary shows >2% increase in 95th latency or >0.5% regression in success rate.
testing_plan: Unit tests for trip_score math and state transitions. Load tests (k6) simulating 429 storms and timeouts to validate hysteresis. Chaos experiment: inject regional latency for 30m and validate variant fallback behavior. Integration tests for model-variant compatibility checks. Run canary with feature-flag and 0-RT rollback path.
rollout_plan: - Phase 1: Internal routes only (1 week). - Phase 2: 10% customer traffic with telemetry gating (2 weeks). - Phase 3: 50% with conservative thresholds (1 week). - Phase 4: Global enable. Rollback criteria: any phase with >2% latency P95 regression or >1% request error increase compared to baseline.
open_questions: - How should we weight 429s vs timeouts in trip_score for mixed workloads? (API clients vs streaming chat) - Should model-variant swap be limited to quantized-compatible variants only, or allow fallback to CPU-hosted variants for extreme cases? - How to surfacing tenant-specific overrides in Console without exposing raw thresholds?
